Appreciate the clear summary and the redlines. Quick responses to your three asks: 
1) Output ownership / assignment: Redwood's standard approach is to grant customers a perpetual, non-exclusive, transferable license to use outputs and to productize them. We don't typically assign title to generated outputs, but we can propose tailored language for customers who require assignment for specific productized artifacts.

2) Training opt-out: We can offer an opt-out for training on Dedicated and Private deployments. For the hosted API, we can agree not to use customer-provided data or customer-specific generated outputs for future model training without explicit consent; however, a limited feedback license for aggregated telemetry is typical (helps maintain service quality).

3) Telemetry / evidence: We can produce redacted request/response traces and retention metadata as part of an evidence package. Ben in Ops will confirm what we can export and timing.

Hi Anna / Priyom,

Thanks for the quick context. Laura from Legal here — copying Acme legal as well. I reviewed the attached redlines and Priyom's proposed language. High-level: we want to stay aligned with Redwood policy while being pragmatic for enterprise productization needs. Proposed positions below for insertion into the MSA / Order Form: 

- Output ownership: Replace a blanket assignment with a narrowly scoped assignment option — Acme may receive assignment of title only to outputs that are (a) uniquely generated for Acme (determinable and segregatable), and (b) explicitly listed in the Order Form as "Assigned Outputs". For all other outputs, Redwood grants a perpetual, royalty-free, non-exclusive, irrevocable license to use, reproduce, modify, and distribute.

- Training & data use: Redwood will not use customer-provided data or customer-labeled outputs to further train or fine-tune models unless Acme expressly opts in. For Hosted plans, we will: (i) treat customer data as not used for model training by default; (ii) allow an opt-in that may be covered by a separate agreement and compensation. For Dedicated/Private, the opt-out is simpler to implement and we can confirm through configuration.

- Feedback license: We can accept an anonymized, aggregated feedback license limited to improvements to the Redwood platform, with explicit exclusions for customer-identifiable outputs and PII.

- Evidence & telemetry: To satisfy audit requirements, Redwood can provide: (i) SOC 2 Type II report; (ii) redacted request/response traces (CSV/Parquet) for a mutually agreed time window; (iii) data flow diagram. We cannot produce raw PII or unretracted customer content. Ben, please confirm export formats and retention windows below.

I'll draft redline language in a follow-up and propose a short two-way call to walk specifics (assignment mechanics, Order Form exhibit for Assigned Outputs, and evidence packaging). Priyom — let's aim to get a working draft to Acme by Tuesday EOD.

Regards,
